sources.publication: Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, The Paris Peace Conference, 1919, Volume II
sources.title: The Secretary of State to the Swiss Minister (Sulzer)
sources.short_quote: also to the Supreme War Council in Paris
sources.paraphrase: Lansing acknowledges German radio requests about the Ottoman and German armistices and states that they will be communicated to the associated governments and the Supreme War Council in Paris.
sources.relevance: Independently corroborates the routing described in p221 B3-B4.

sources.publication: Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, The Paris Peace Conference, 1919, Volume II
sources.title: The Secretary of State to the Special Representative (House)
sources.short_quote: German civilians being permitted to remain in Turkey
sources.paraphrase: Lansing sends House, for the Supreme War Council, Solf’s November 15 wireless request that German civilians be allowed to remain in the Ottoman Empire despite the armistice evacuation provision.
sources.relevance: Independently corroborates the specific civilian-residence request described in p221 B3-B4.

limits: These are contemporary diplomatic texts reproduced in an official U.S. source edition; the underlying manuscript documents were not inspected.
They do not identify the 0YY headcount, confirm that those civilians had departed, resolve source-coordinate gaps, or establish the date of any particular civilian transport.
The German intercepted message credits President Wilson; the corroborating documents record Lansing’s official actions. This does not establish a separate personal act by Wilson.
